problems.title: A parallel line through a point
problems.question: Find the line through(2,15) parallel to y=7x−8.
problems.idea: Use the defining equation or geometric theorem, and verify the resulting value.
formulas: Parallel nonvertical lines have the same slope.
steps: Write y=7x+b. Substitution gives 15=14+b, so b=1.

problems.title: Perpendicular slope through the origin
problems.question: Find the line perpendicular to y=5x+4 through the origin.
problems.idea: Use the defining equation or geometric theorem, and verify the resulting value.
formulas: Perpendicular slopes multiply to −1.
steps: The required slope is −1/5 and its intercept is 0.

problems.title: Evaluate and add function values
problems.question: For g(x)=4x+8, find g(2)+g(−3).
problems.idea: Use the defining equation or geometric theorem, and verify the resulting value.
steps: Their sum is 12.

problems.title: Reverse a translation
problems.question: The translation taking A(3,7) to B(−1,8) takes which point to C(−9,5)?
problems.idea: Use the defining equation or geometric theorem, and verify the resulting value.
formulas: The translation vector is B−A=(−4,1).
steps: Subtract it from the destination:(−9,5)−(−4,1)=(−5,4).

problems.title: A diameter bisects a perpendicular chord
problems.question: AB is a diameter, AC=12, BAC=30°, and chord CD is perpendicular to AB. Find CD.
problems.idea: Use the defining equation or geometric theorem, and verify the resulting value.
formulas: If H=AB∩CD, then CH=ACsin30°=6 and CH=HD.
steps: A centre-to-chord perpendicular bisects the chord. Hence CD=2·6=12.

problems.title: Substitution in two linear equations
problems.question: Solve3x−y=7,2x+3y=12 and find x+y.
problems.idea: Use the defining equation or geometric theorem, and verify the resulting value.
formulas: From the first equation, y=3x−7.
steps: Substitution gives 2x+9x−21=12, so x=3, y=2. Thus x+y=5.

problems.title: Alternating quotient of odd powers
problems.question: How many terms has the quotient of a⁷+1 by a+1?
problems.idea: Use the defining equation or geometric theorem, and verify the resulting value.
steps: The quotient contains the seven powers from degree6 through degree0, with alternating signs.

problems.title: Use the shared graph point
problems.question: Lines y=ax+b and y=cx+d meet at(1,1). Find |(a+b)³−(c+d)²|.
problems.idea: Use the defining equation or geometric theorem, and verify the resulting value.
formulas: Substitution givesa+b=c+d=1.
steps: Thus the requested value is|1³−1²|=0.

problems.title: Equal tangents form an equilateral triangle
problems.question: MA, MB are tangents from M to a circle of centre O. OMA=30° and MA+MB=18. Find AB.
problems.idea: Use the defining equation or geometric theorem, and verify the resulting value.
formulas: Tangents from one point are equal, and OM bisects the angle between them.
steps: Thus MA=MB=9 and AMB=60°. An isosceles triangle with apex60° is equilateral.
Therefore AB=9.

problems.title: Two tangent circles in a sixty-degree wedge
problems.question: Two circles touch both sides of a 60° angle and each other externally. One radius is 12. Which listed other radius is possible?
problems.idea: Use the defining equation or geometric theorem, and verify the resulting value.
formulas: Their centre distances from the vertex are twice their radii. Thus2(R−r)=R+r, giving R=3r.
steps: The other radius can be4 or 36. Only 36 is listed.

problems.title: Infinite solutions require proportional equations
problems.question: The system mx+3y=8,5x+ny=4 has infinitely many solutions. Find mn.
problems.idea: Use the defining equation or geometric theorem, and verify the resulting value.
formulas: The first equation must be twice the second, because8=2·4.
steps: Thus m=10 and 3=2n, so n=3/2. Product mn=15.

problems.title: Check factorisations against triangle inequalities
problems.question: For triangle sides a, b, c, how many of the six printed equalities can hold?
problems.idea: Use the defining equation or geometric theorem, and verify the resulting value.
formulas: Triangle inequalities require a+b>c, a+c>b, b+c>a.
steps: The first factors to(a+b)(a²−ab+b²)=c(a²−ab+b²), forcing a+b=c. The second givesc=a+2b, and the thirdc=a+(5/4)b. All are impossible.
The fourth givesa−b=c. The fifth factors to a(b+c)=(c−b)(b+c), again forcing a+b=c. Both are impossible.
The sixth divides bybc>0 to givea+c=2b, which is possible, for examplea=b=c=1. Thus exactly one equality can hold.

problems.title: Compare exponents and coefficients in an identity
problems.question: Positive integersm, n satisfy(−2a^n b^n)^m+(3a^m b^m)^n=a⁶b⁶ identically. Find m³+n³.
problems.idea: Use the defining equation or geometric theorem, and verify the resulting value.
formulas: Exponent comparison givesmn=6; coefficient comparison gives(−2)^m+3^n=1.
steps: Thus m³+n³=27+8=35.

problems.title: An inscribed angle from two arcs
problems.question: ArcsMN, MK have measures72°,32°. Which listed value can angle KMN have?
problems.idea: Use the defining equation or geometric theorem, and verify the resulting value.
formulas: Put K on the 72° arc MN,32° from M. Then the arc KN avoiding M has measure72°−32°=40°.
steps: The inscribed angle KMN is half its intercepted arc, so it can equal20°.
problems.note: The relative placement of K, N also permits another configuration; the question asks which listed value is possible.

problems.title: Farthest points on externally tangent circles
problems.question: Two externally tangent circles have radii5,7. Maximise AB with one point on each circle.
problems.idea: Use the defining equation or geometric theorem, and verify the resulting value.
formulas: Centre distance=5+7=12. By the triangle inequality, AB≤5+12+7.
steps: Take the outermost points on the common centre line to attain the bound24.

problems.title: Reflect two points across the horizontal axis
problems.question: Find the line through the reflections of A(−1,3), B(1,9) across Ox.
problems.idea: Use the defining equation or geometric theorem, and verify the resulting value.
formulas: Reflection sends(x, y) to(x,−y), giving(−1,−3),(1,−9).
steps: The slope is(−9+3)/(1+1)=−3. Substitution gives intercept−6.

problems.title: Choose the positive quadratic root
problems.question: For positivea, a²+4a−21=0. Find a.
problems.idea: Use the defining equation or geometric theorem, and verify the resulting value.
steps: The roots are −7 and 3. Positivity selects3.

problems.title: Remaining work gives one worker’s rate
problems.question: Two workers together need12 days. After8 days, one leaves and the other finishes in7 more. Find their separate times.
problems.idea: Use the defining equation or geometric theorem, and verify the resulting value.
formulas: Together they complete8/12=2/3, leaving1/3. The remaining worker’s rate is(1/3)/7=1/21.
steps: The other worker’s rate is 1/12−1/21=1/28.
Their separate completion times are 21 and 28 days.

problems.title: A diameter makes the altitude to an isosceles base
problems.question: AB is an equal leg of isosceles triangle ABC with base AC. The circle of diameter AB meets AC again at M. If MC=8, find AM.
problems.idea: Use the defining equation or geometric theorem, and verify the resulting value.
formulas: AngleAMB=90° because it subtends diameter AB. Thus BM is the altitude from the isosceles apex B.
steps: That altitude bisects the base AC, so AM=MC=8.

problems.title: A diameter makes two lines perpendicular
problems.question: Line y=4x+12 meets Ox at A; line y=ax+b meets Ox at B(4,0). Their intersection lies on the circle of diameter AB. Find a+b.
problems.idea: Use the defining equation or geometric theorem, and verify the resulting value.
formulas: The inscribed angle at their intersection is 90°, so the slopes satisfy4a=−1.
steps: Thus a=−1/4. Since(4,0) lies on the second line,0=4a+b givesb=1.
Therefore a+b=3/4.

problems.title: Even and odd counts in a consecutive block
problems.question: In a block of consecutive positive integers,52% are even. Find the number of even integers.
problems.idea: Use the defining equation or geometric theorem, and verify the resulting value.
formulas: Write the total as25k, with 13k even and 12k odd. Consecutive blocks have even/odd counts differing by at most1.
steps: Their difference is k, so k=1. Thus the block has 13 even numbers.

problems.title: No solution at the singular coefficient values
problems.question: Find the product of allm making |m−7|x+2y=m−5,2x+y=30 inconsistent.
problems.idea: Use the defining equation or geometric theorem, and verify the resulting value.
formulas: The determinant is|m−7|−4; it vanishes only for m=3 or 11.
steps: At these values, the first left side is twice the second, so consistency would requirem−5=60. Neither value satisfies that.
Both are inconsistent; their product is 3·11=33.

problems.title: Cancel a nonzero difference
problems.question: Distinct nonzeroa, b satisfy a/b+a=b/a+b. Find 1/a+1/b.
problems.idea: Use the defining equation or geometric theorem, and verify the resulting value.
steps: The equation becomes(a−b)(a+b)/(ab)=−(a−b). Sincea≠b, divide bya−b.
The result is(a+b)/(ab)=−1, which equals 1/a+1/b.

problems.title: Inscribed angle from a circle in a wedge
problems.question: Two circles in angle S=θ touch externally at D and the same side at A, B, with B nearer S. BD meets the larger circle again at C. If ACB=θ, find θ.
problems.idea: Use the defining equation or geometric theorem, and verify the resulting value.
formulas: The centres and D lie on the wedge bisector. The large-circle radius toward A is perpendicular to the side, so its smaller angle with the radius toward D is 90°−θ/2.
steps: The inscribed angle ACB intercepts arc AD, so it equals(90°−θ/2)/2=45°−θ/4.
The given equality givesθ=45°−θ/4, so 5θ/4=45° andθ=36°.

problems.title: Use a common tangent and two inscribed angles
problems.question: Two externally tangent circles in equilateral triangle ABC both touch AC. They touch AB at M, BC at N, and one another at K. Find MKN.
problems.idea: Use the defining equation or geometric theorem, and verify the resulting value.
formulas: Let their contacts on AC be P, Q. Their common tangent at K meets AC at T; equal tangents give TP=TK=TQ.
steps: ThusT is the midpoint of PQ and K lies on the circle of diameter PQ, so PKQ=90°.
The radii toward M, P make120°, as do those toward N, Q, because the triangle’s base angles are 60°. The inscribed angles MKP and NKQ are therefore60° each.
The four angles around K sum to 360°. Hence MKN=360°−60°−90°−60°=150°.
